subject: Model selection & context-length: hourly token projection request
messages:
From: Emma Soto <emma@finbridge.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model selection & context-length: hourly token projection request

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — FinBridge is excited about bringing Redwood into our document summarization and anomaly-detection pipelines. Before we move the SOW forward, procurement needs a model shortlist and an hourly token estimate so we can size reserved capacity for the first 90 days.

Quick background: our ingestion pipeline emits ~3.2M raw documents per month. For the initial scope we plan to run: (1) extractive summarization of individual docs (avg 1.6k chars), (2) short chat assists for analyst queries (avg 60 tokens per chat), and (3) a nightly batch pass that produces anomaly flags across aggregated time windows. We expect peak traffic between 09:00–13:00 PT on weekdays.

Can your team propose 2–3 model variants (one accuracy-first, one cost-optimized, one balanced) with recommended max context lengths and a conservative hourly token projection (peak & median) for the initial 90-day ramp? Attaching a CSV with a sample token distribution (FinBridge_Q3_Token_Report.csv).

Also include any guidance on cache/prefix strategies — we have a lot of repeated headers and templates.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Soto
Senior Data Platform Manager
FinBridge Analytics

Attachment: FinBridge_Q3_Token_Report.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Soto <emma@finbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model selection & context-length: hourly token projection request

Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the token CSV. Looping in Marissa (CS) and Monica (solutions) to help with sizing and the SOW.

High level we recommend the following shortlist for the initial run: 
- Variant A (accuracy-first): Redwood-1-large, 32k context — best for multi-document summarization and nightly analytics joins.
- Variant B (balanced): Redwood-1-medium, 16k context — good latency/cost tradeoff for chat + summarization.
- Variant C (cost-optimized): OpenLite-v1 (quantized), 8k context — for high-throughput chat and batched processing where extreme accuracy is not critical.

Preliminary hourly token projection (based on your CSV + conservative user patterns):
- Median hour: ~420k tokens/hour
- Peak hour: ~1.1M tokens/hour (09:00–11:00 PT window)
- Nightly batch (2–3am): ~2.8M tokens in a single 90-minute window (batched jobs)

Cache notes: prefix-based caching on repeated header blocks should reduce tokenized input by ~10–20% for summaries. We can instrument a lightweight prefix fingerprint in the adapter to validate that in early rollout.

Action items: 
1) Marissa — can you draft a short capacity plan and SOW attachment for the procurement team (include dedicated burst capacity and canary policy)?
2) Monica — can you run a quick microbench (16k vs 32k) with the sample_payloads.json to confirm latency at target p95?

Emma — will follow up with a one-pager and a numeric table for procurement.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-10-25T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model selection & context-length: hourly token projection request

Hi all — attaching a draft SOW and a token heatmap that maps the CSV rows to our recommended hourly bands. Key points for procurement:
- For a 90-day ramp we recommend starting with a Reserved Dedicated pool sized for the median hour and 30% burst capacity for the peak window.
- Canary: route 5% traffic to Redwood-1-large for the first 2 weeks to validate summarization quality against a blind eval set.
- Autoscale policy: scale in 10-minute windows for batch jobs, 1–2 second windows for chat routes.

Attachments: SOW_Draft_v1.pdf, token_heatmap.png (see linked drive for large image).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — attaching the sample payloads you asked for (sample_payloads.json). A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The 1.6k-char summaries are often single-document, but ~12% require cross-doc context (those would benefit from 32k).
- We expect 1–2k concurrent chat sessions during peak; each chat session averages 4 messages per minute when active.

Procurement also asked for a simple cost table comparing: (A) hosted per-token, (B) dedicated reserved (monthly commit model), (C) estimated cost for quantized OpenLite at projected peak. If you can add that to the SOW that would help speed approvals.

Attachment: sample_payloads.json (JSON, 450 KB)
